overclaim_search_hits.text: The M4 runtime estimator first takes each condition's median of \RTReps\ repetitions, then forms a prompt latency ratio and its geometric mean across \RTPrompts\ prompts. The offline oracle uses the smaller target-only or Always-Spec median for each prompt. Bootstrap intervals use \RTBootstrap\ draws with Python Random seed \RTSeed, resampling prompts in the frozen held-out order. Percentile endpoints linearly interpolate the sorted bootstrap draws at quantiles .025 and .975. A single random stream computes Target/Guard, Target/Always-Spec, and Guard/oracle intervals in that order. This preserves the frozen finite-bootstrap calculation; it does not replace the hardware estimators in Table~\ref{tab:statistics}. Intervals condition on the selected policy and observed prompt medians; they do not incorporate recalibration or between-session variation. The oracle selects between two measured fixed conditions, not all possible switching policies, so it is not a universal latency lower bound.

Calibration, qualification, and held-out IDs are disjoint. Selection ranks tasks with no recorded prior M4 exposure in the frozen inventory by a seeded hash within each of HumanEval and Spec-Bench; each split is balanced across these two families. The registered grid has nine candidates: first decision round $E\in\{2,4,8\}$ and margin $m\in\{0,0.05,0.10\}$. Calibration selects the exact candidate with the lowest geometric-mean latency ratio to the offline oracle. Exact ties break by mean measured guard-compute overhead, smaller exploration count, larger margin, and lexicographic candidate ID. The frozen winner is \texttt{E8\_M000}; held-out results never select or retune it.

The reference is the median across calibration prompts of each prompt's median target latency divided by its median output-token count. The preregistered candidate grid varies the first decision round and margin. Selection minimizes calibration geometric-mean latency relative to the offline minimum of target-only and Always-Spec among exact candidates, with frozen tie-breaks. The selected rule uses margin \RTMargin\ and first decides after \RTRounds\ completed speculative rounds; it then decides after each later round while speculation continues. A request ending earlier makes no decision. The online policy receives neither task/family labels nor future output length, current-request target-only latency, or oracle outcomes.
